summary: The incident is most likely caused by config change cfg-2207, which cut portfolio-service's datasource pool (db.pool.max_size 50->5) at 09:52Z and saturated portfolio-service, propagating upstream as gateway 504s on /v1/portfolio/* (H2, confidence 0.60, medium). The onset evidence is the strongest discriminator: gateway and portfolio-service p99 both jump in the same 09:50-09:52Z bucket and then hold ~4.3s, and cfg-2207 is the only change at that moment, whereas the gateway HTTP/2 deploy (dep-5220) preceded onset by 110 minutes with flat latency in between (H1 downgraded to 0.12). Confidence is medium rather than high because no metric or log data was retrieved from portfolio-service's own pool/CPU metrics or from the shared datastores (ledger-db, redis-cache), so an independent datastore fault (H3, 0.22) cannot be fully excluded. Recommendation: roll back cfg-2207 first (fast, low-risk, directly tests the top hypothesis), and if latency does not recover, escalate to datastore-layer checks before touching the gateway deploy.

ranked_hypotheses.title: cfg-2207 portfolio-service DB pool cut (50->5) exhausted its ledger-db connection pool, saturating portfolio-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-2207 ('Apply cost-optimisation profile small', db.pool.max_size 50->5) at 09:52Z shrank portfolio-service's datasource pool, so portfolio-service requests queue/block waiting for a connection to ledger-db, driving portfolio-service latency to ~4.3s and propagating upstream as gateway 504s on /v1/portfolio/*.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2207 changes portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5 at 09:52Z via an automated cost-optimisation profile
With only 5 pooled connections, portfolio-service requests block/queue on the ledger-db pool (pool exhaustion), the same mechanism as the matching precedent HIST-115
portfolio-service p99 jumps in the 09:50Z bucket alongside the gateway, showing the latency originates inside the portfolio-service path
Slow portfolio-service calls exceed the gateway upstream timeout -> 504s confined to /v1/portfolio/holdings

assumptions: cfg-2207 propagates promptly (pool resize applied on reload) rather than only at next restart
The 09:52 config commit and the 09:50-09:52 metric onset offset is measurement-bucket granularity, not a genuine 2-minute lead of the symptom over the cause

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared ledger-db (or redis-cache) degraded independently of any change, slowing portfolio-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared datastore on the portfolio path — ledger-db (shared:true) or redis-cache (shared:true) — began failing or throttling (as in HIST-102 failover / HIST-110 IOPS throttling) around 09:50Z, so portfolio-service calls blocked on the datastore and the gateway reflected the upstream wait as 504s. No change was recorded for these components.

ledger-db or redis-cache degrades (failover, IOPS throttling, connection saturation) around 09:50Z
portfolio-service requests block on the degraded datastore -> p99 ~4.3s
Gateway surfaces the upstream wait as 504s on /v1/portfolio/holdings

The datastore would produce no ERROR-level gateway logs, only upstream timeouts

api-gateway p99 stays flat at ~200-230 ms and error_rate at 0.17-0.31%; portfolio-service p99 stays flat at ~170-190 ms — no impact from the 08:00Z gateway deploy for the first 105+ minutes (F7, F9, F12).

Onset: gateway p99 jumps in the 09:50Z bucket (avg 1849.99 ms, max 4418.76) and error_rate rises to 1.66% avg; portfolio-service p99 rises in the SAME bucket (avg 1865.15 ms, max 4546.3) (F7, F8, F9, F12).

Gateway 504/timeout WARN entries first seen 09:53:53Z, all confined to /v1/portfolio/holdings ('upstream timeout portfolio-service'); gateway p99 holds ~4300 ms and error_rate ~7.1-7.3% through 11:55Z (F7, F9, F10).
Incident INC-002 reported by on-call SRE: portfolio page spinning/timing out, gateway p99 through the roof, suspicion placed on the morning gateway HTTP/2 upgrade.
Latest data: no rollback of dep-5220 and no revert of cfg-2207 recorded; degradation persists (F6, F13).

recommended_actions.action: Revert config change cfg-2207 (portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 5 -> 50) and watch api-gateway and portfolio-service p99 over the next 10 minutes.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 is the only change coincident with the 09:50-09:52Z onset, and the top hypothesis (H2, 0.60) attributes the saturation to a pool cut via a profile; a config revert is fast, low-risk and directly tests the leading hypothesis. HIST-115 shows the same 'wrong environment profile cut the datasource pool' pattern with fix 'Reverted config'.

recommended_actions.action: While the revert propagates, verify portfolio-service db_pool_in_use, cpu_pct, memory_pct, restarts and its WARN/ERROR logs over 09:40-10:00Z, and pull ledger-db/redis-cache connection-pool, IOPS and GC telemetry for the same window.
recommended_actions.rationale: Distinguishes H2 (pool exhausted in portfolio-service) from H3 (shared datastore degraded independently). These metrics were never retrieved, which is the main reason confidence is capped at medium.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back dep-5220 (the gateway HTTP/2 upgrade) as a first move; if p99 remains elevated after the cfg-2207 revert, then roll back api-gateway to v9.3.0-predecessor and re-measure /v1/portfolio/* latency.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 08:00Z deploy preceded onset by 110 minutes with flat latency in between, so it requires an implausible delayed trigger; rolling it back first would discard the stronger causal evidence and add avoidable risk. It stays as the fallback if the pool revert fails.

recommended_actions.action: If neither revert restores latency, capture a live latency profile of portfolio-service -> ledger-db (connection acquisition wait time vs query time) and check ledger-db for primary failover or I/O throttling, per the HIST-102 / HIST-110 patterns.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the discriminating step for the remaining H3 datastore-degradation hypothesis, which could not be ruled in or out from change data alone.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm fix: verify p99 returns to ~200 ms baseline on both api-gateway and portfolio-service and that gateway 504s on /v1/portfolio/holdings cease, then close the incident with the confirmed cause.
recommended_actions.rationale: Establishes causal validation (a step explicitly missing from the evidence) and ensures the degradation has fully cleared before declaring resolution.

recommended_actions.action: Add guardrails on datasource pool configuration: require a minimum pool size floor per service class and enforce change review/validation for 'cost-optimisation profile' configs applied by automation to request-path services.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence of the HIST-115 failure mode ('datasource pool size overridden by a wrong environment profile'); cfg-2207 was committed by infra-automation with no validation gate.

recommended_actions.action: Add per-service alerting on db_pool_in_use / connection-acquisition latency and a golden-signal alert keyed to /v1/portfolio/* so pool exhaustion is caught before it manifests as gateway 504s.
recommended_actions.rationale: The incident was detected only at the gateway edge (504s, p99) after portfolio-service was already saturated; portfolio-service exposes db_pool_in_use but no alert fired on it.

data_gaps: get_service_dependencies for api-gateway direction=upstream returned empty, so callers in front of the gateway (DNS/LB/mesh) could not be enumerated; cannot confirm whether any component upstream of the gateway changed in the window (limits rejection of H4).

No metric time series were retrieved for api-gateway, portfolio-service, ledger-db or redis-cache (tool budget exhausted); cannot establish exact onset ordering within the 09:50-09:52Z bucket, nor whether the shared datastores themselves degraded.

portfolio-service's own resource metrics (cpu_pct, memory_pct, db_pool_in_use, GC) and its WARN/ERROR logs were never queried, although the metric list exists; cannot directly confirm pool exhaustion as opposed to other in-service saturation — this is the biggest gap in supporting H2.
No telemetry for ledger-db or redis-cache (connection-pool saturation, IOPS, GC); H3 cannot be excluded from data, only from the absence of a recorded change.
Deployment records exist only for api-gateway; an unrecorded binary/config rollout on the shared datastores cannot be fully ruled out.
No explicit effective-propagation time for cfg-2207 (commit vs pod reload of db.pool.max_size), so the 09:52 commit cannot be perfectly reconciled with the 09:50 metric bucket onset.

Blast-radius confirmation for non-portfolio routes relied on a truncated log-pattern summary (40 of 252 rows returned); absence of other routes in the timeout signature is well-supported but not exhaustively verified.
No post-change validation data exists for a rollback of cfg-2207 or dep-5220; no remediation event appears in the change list, so neither candidate change has been causally validated by recovery.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: portfolio-service db_pool_in_use rising to/near the new limit of 5 at 09:50Z with no evidence of a datastore-side fault would strongly confirm H2 and raise confidence to high.
Latency persisting unchanged after reverting cfg-2207 would falsify H2 as the sole cause and shift weight to H1 (gateway HTTP/2) or H3 (datastore degradation).

Evidence of ledger-db failover, connection refusals, or I/O throttling beginning at ~09:50Z (HIST-102/HIST-110 pattern) while portfolio-service's pool was never saturated would overturn H2 in favor of H3.
Finding that cfg-2207's pool resize only takes effect at next pod restart (i.e., it had not yet applied by 10:05Z) would remove it as the cause and strengthen H1 or H3.

A delayed gateway-side HTTP/2 effect (e.g., connection-reuse exhaustion or a stream-limit hit appearing only after ~110 minutes of traffic, or evidence of upstream resets in gateway logs) would overturn the timing argument and support H1.

Portfolio-service p99 rising strictly before gateway p99 with matching service-internal metrics would confirm the latency originates inside portfolio-service; the reverse (gateway-first) would point to the gateway or the network path in front of it (H4).
